name: Pistol Squat
summary: An advanced unilateral bodyweight exercise where one squats to full depth on a single leg with the opposite leg held straight out in front.

setup: Stand tall on one leg with your feet pointing forward.
Extend the opposite leg out in front of you, keeping the knee straight and toes pointed up.
Reach your arms forward at shoulder height to assist with balance.
steps: Inhale and initiate the descent by breaking at the hip and knee simultaneously on the working leg.
Lower yourself under control as deep as mobility allows, keeping the non-working leg elevated off the floor.
Pause briefly at the bottom without bouncing or losing balance.
Drive firmly through the whole foot to extend the knee and hip back to the starting standing position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply during the descent and exhale forcefully as you drive out of the bottom to stand up.
cues: Reach forward with your hands to counterbalance your hips.
Keep the working heel glued to the floor.
Actively lift the front leg to keep it clear of the ground.

common_faults.fault: Working heel elevating off the floor.
common_faults.correction: Improve ankle dorsiflexion mobility, or elevate the heel slightly on a small wedge while developing range.

common_faults.fault: Knee caving inward into valgus during ascent.
common_faults.correction: Actively engage the gluteus medius and track the knee directly in line with the middle toes.

common_faults.fault: The non-working foot dragging or touching the floor.
common_faults.correction: Engage the hip flexors and quadriceps of the non-working leg to hold it parallel to the ground.

precautions: Avoid collapsing abruptly into the bottom position, as this places heavy compressive forces on the knee joint.
